Yes.
Tell me how.
Train to our stop. If train is closed, bus to the church with the blue door. Three blocks past the fruit man. Turn at the laundromat.
I did not teach her that way.
No.

dialogueInline.text: Do you independently procure ordinary household necessities without caseworker facilitation?
I know the words. I do not know why you put them in that order.
Do you buy things the household needs by yourself?
Yes. Food. Soap. Needles. Coffee when Bjorn forgets.
I do not forget coffee.
You forget other people drink it.

summary: Astrid's answer to a blunt ordinary question accumulates into the most self-directed daily life in the household precisely because no single activity is impressive.

dialogueInline.text: What do you do on a normal day when Ms. Carrie is not with you?
Laundry. Food. I see upstairs woman. Sometimes park.
I buy what is missing. I bring back what I borrow. I walk when I want quiet.
Then I go home.

directionInline.text: Ordinary-life cutaways are reader-facing illustrations, not projected evidence. Keep Astrid's routine mundane and self-directed.

summary: Carrie, Gunnar, and Bjorn realize together that Astrid needed less management than anyone because her successful integration became almost invisible.

panelPlan.action: Wide. Astrid sits calmly after answering. No one announces a conclusion.
Carrie looks from Astrid to her file.
Gunnar looks at Astrid, then at his own transit card peeking from his pocket.
Bjorn watches Astrid with a complicated mix of pride and recognition that he did not know this part of her life.
Hearing Officer simply turns the page. The procedural normality makes the realization larger for the reader than for the room.
